page.layout: One page of text. At the top, four lines of Syriac in full width, then an italic Latin paragraph, then a Latin line with Syriac continuing below it, down to the foot of the text block. Page number at the top right. No running head, no margin notes, no catchword.

p.i: Non enim ut reponantur divini libri in fenestris, scripti sunt; & neque ut sicut cantilena, & Parabola quedam mundana occinantur in Ecclesia: Sed ut ne unum quidem ex eis cadat super terram, & ut sicut pupilla oculi custodiantur.

main_text.p: Timotheus item Nestorianorum Patriarcha in sua Nationali Synodo Can. 1. hoc idem afferit: [illegible, ~150 letters]

page.notes: The Syriac passages are not transcribed: the letters are too small and faint on this scan to read reliably, so they are marked as illegible with approximate letter counts. The top Syriac block is not marked as a continuation, as the scan does not show whether it goes on from the previous page. A stray pen stroke near the lower centre of the text block is handwriting and was left out. The Latin paragraph has been changed to u/v spelling ("ut", "unum", "divini"), as the rules require. The printed "quedam" is kept as it stands.
